messages:
alex_sales: quick heads-up — running a POC with Finlytics, streaming responses from our hosted API hang for them when using the TS SDK with `stream: true`. customer is behind a corporate proxy/firewall. they see no chunks until the entire response completes, then the client gets everything at once. this kills UX.

maria_se: thanks alex. which SDK version and node/browser? any error logs or a minimal repro?

sam_dev: can you paste the TS snippet they're using? often it's a fetch/net polyfill issue in node.

alex_sales: sdk 0.19.2, node 18.16.0. snippet from their app (typescript):

```ts
const r = await client.responses.create({
  model: 'redwood-std-v1',
  input: 'stream me tokens',
  stream: true,
});
for await (const chunk of r.stream()) {
  render(chunk);
}
```

They say everything buffers for ~10s and then a single big chunk arrives.

jordan_sre: classic corporate-proxy-buffering symptom — some proxies buffer responses until they see `Content-Length` or the connection closes. chunked transfers (`Transfer-Encoding: chunked`) should stream, but if the proxy removes/chunks incorrectly you get buffering. can you confirm the HTTP response headers from our server as seen by their proxy? tcpdump or curl from their network would help.

maria_se: quick troubleshooting steps: 1) try curl w/ streaming from inside their network: `curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood.ai/responses..."` 2) capture headers `-i` 3) ask proxy team if they rewrite/insert `Content-Length` or disable chunked.

sam_dev: another thing — node fetch libs sometimes need `duplex: 'half'` for streaming bodies with fetch in Node 18+ (when using a streamable request body). not usually for response streaming but sometimes polyfills cause buffering. if they're using `undici`/`node-fetch` wrapper, try a plain `curl` test first.

jordan_sre: sharing a quick curl repro to run from their laptop (replace URL):

```bash
# run inside corporate network where issue reproduces
curl -v -N \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/responses?model=redwood-std-v1&input=stream-test"
```

Look at `Transfer-Encoding` vs `Content-Length` and how long between first byte and final byte. If the first byte arrives immediately but the app buffers, that's client-side. If nothing arrives until the end, proxy likely buffering.

olivia_pm: customer also pressed on pricing for streaming — wants to know if enabling streaming changes cost buckets or billing visibility. alex, can you capture their use-case (tokens per minute) so we can give ballpark?

alex_sales: they expect ~200 req/min with median 400 tokens per response, spike to 1k. they need predictability for cost. also security questionnaire flagged IP allowlist + SSO + data retention. those are separate but blocking enterprise sign-off.

maria_se: on pricing — streaming doesn't change token billing. they still pay per generated token. streaming only affects client latency and UX. for predictability advise dedicated capacity/committed plan if they need strict SLAs for spikes.

jordan_sre: immediate mitigations: ask customer proxy team to allow `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` passthrough or whitelist `api.redwood.ai`. longer term: enable websocket streaming option (we have a websocket endpoint that bypasses some corporate HTTP proxies) — this often fixes corporate buffering. I can prepare an internal note on websocket endpoint and firewall rules.

sam_dev: if customer wants a quick app workaround: in TS, use low-level fetch and stream body manually, force flushing on each token in our SDK (we can push a short-lived patch to increase flush frequency from runtime side). Also try the websocket path if their infra allows outbound ws to our domain.

alex_sales: ok i'll ask them to run the curl command and forward pcap / tcpdump if they can. they may need approval from their security team.

maria_se: also ask them to run this tcpdump (one-liner) while reproducing so we can see wire-level behavior: `sudo tcpdump -i any -s 0 -w streaming-proxy.pcap host api.redwood.ai` and share the pcap via secure link.

ajordan_sre: added: if we confirm the proxy injects `Content-Length`, we should offer a short-term workaround: enable websocket or provide a demo build of our SDK that sends frequent flushes (lower buffer interval). i'll own the internal PR if needed.

olivia_pm: next steps for sales: 1) get curl + headers 2) get pcap or proxy team confirmation 3) capture tokens/min for pricing rec. i'll join the sync with Finlytics tomorrow.

alex_sales: thanks all — i'll ping back with curl output and whether the proxy team will allow ws. :thumbsup:
